nodes.title: PICTURE 1 | PRIMARY TARGET — choose your photo
PICTURE 2 | PRIMARY REFERENCE — donor / style / scene
Final canvas = Picture 1 ratio × output MP
H3 edit prompt | FACE SWAP | Universal 16
widgets_values:
Edit <Picture 1>. Replace the facial identity of the main person with the facial identity from <Picture 2>.

<Picture 1> defines the original photograph, including the scene, camera perspective, head orientation, hairstyle, accessories, clothing, body, lighting, and background.

<Picture 2> provides the facial identity of the replacement person, including eye shape and spacing, nose, lips, cheekbones, jawline, facial proportions, skin characteristics, and distinctive facial details.

Transfer the facial identity from <Picture 2> with maximum accuracy and fidelity, preserving the recognizable features and unique characteristics of the reference person.

Create one natural, believable photograph in which the person from <Picture 2> appears in the scene from <Picture 1>.

Adapt the transferred face naturally to the original head orientation, expression, perspective, and lighting.

Allow subtle adjustments to the surrounding facial contours, hairline, nearby hair strands, shadows, and skin transitions wherever necessary to achieve a seamless and anatomically coherent result.

Preserve the overall hairstyle, hair color, hair length, and appearance from <Picture 1>, but allow minor natural adjustments to accommodate the replacement face.

Hair from <Picture 2> must not be transferred as part of the facial identity. Any bangs, fringe, or hair covering the reference face should be treated as separate from the facial features.

Avoid overlapping hairstyles, duplicated hair, ghosting, unnatural facial boundaries, or a pasted-on appearance.

Preserve the original accessories, clothing, body, background, and overall composition.

Prioritize accurate facial identity and natural visual integration over rigid pixel-level preservation.

The final result must look like a genuine photograph, not a digitally pasted face.

nodes.title: START HERE — FACE SWAP | UNIVERSAL 16
widgets_values:
1) Picture 1 = primary target. Picture 2 = primary donor / reference.
2) This UNIVERSAL 16 variant keeps the same tested prompt and sampler settings.
3) It removes mandatory pre-resizing of reference images: output MP is controlled independently.
4) The H3 node can accept up to 16 total pictures (Picture 1–16).
5) Your current prompt still references Picture 1 and Picture 2 only; additional pictures are available if you later extend the prompt manually.

nodes.title: IMPORTANT — Universal 16 reference mode
widgets_values:
REFERENCE MODE: UNIVERSAL 16 / DIRECT INPUTS.
Picture 1 and Picture 2 go directly into MiniMaxH3ImageConditioning.
Use this version when you want a cleaner base for scaling from 2 pictures to more references without forcing every reference through the same MP prep path.

nodes.title: HOW TO USE EXTRA PICTURES — 3 to 16
widgets_values:
The MiniMax H3 conditioning node already exposes up to 16 picture inputs.

Default tested mapping in this workflow:
- Picture 1 = main target
- Picture 2 = main donor / reference

Additional pictures:
- Picture 3 to Picture 16 can be connected manually by adding more Load Image nodes and plugging them into the corresponding H3 inputs.
- They are NOT required for the current tested prompts.
- They become useful only if you intentionally edit the prompt to refer to them.

Recommendation:
- Keep only the references that are actually useful.
- More references can increase VRAM/RAM use and may reduce clarity if the prompt does not define each image role clearly.
